symptom: feeling full after just a few bites for months
hook: the stomach had shrunk into a stiff narrow leather bottle
whatYouSee: The stomach is shrunk into a narrow rigid tube with stiff walls and no folds like a leather bottle.
whyItMatters: Linitis plastica is gastric cancer that spreads through the submucosa and makes the wall fixed and narrow. Most patients present with advanced disease.
treatment: Endoscopy with biopsy and CT staging guide care. Surgery with chemotherapy may suit localised disease while advanced disease gets palliative care.
takeaway: A small rigid tube-like stomach on barium is linitis plastica until proven otherwise.

findings: Frontal (AP/PA) upper GI contrast study of the lower chest and abdomen with barium opacifying the esophagus, stomach and proximal duodenal bulb.
The esophagus is a smooth, narrow barium column running along the left of the spine to the gastroesophageal junction, without a clear stricture or filling defect.
The stomach is a narrow, elongated, vertically oriented tubular structure in the left upper abdomen, with a flat upper contour and an air-fluid or barium level under the left hemidiaphragm.
A small rounded barium collection with irregular trailing margins lies inferomedially, likely the pylorus/duodenal bulb or antrum, connected by a thin channel.
The stomach reaches the level of the lower lumbar spine/pelvic brim region with a J- or tubular configuration and no obvious wall mass.
Gas-filled bowel loops in the right and left abdomen, with no obvious obstruction or free air.
The spine is straight and the ribs and lung bases are visible; the lungs are clear on visible portions.
differential: Normal variant vertically oriented, narrow (steerhorn or J-shaped) stomach with a normal pyloroduodenal outflow
Gastric outlet narrowing, such as pyloric stenosis or a peptic or antral stricture, with delayed emptying
Gastric hypotonia or ptosis, or a postoperative or extrinsic compression pattern
anatomyConcerns: No impossible anatomy identified; the tubular, vertical stomach is within the range of normal variation or reflects functional/positional change.
The exact projection (AP vs PA) and patient position cannot be confirmed; the left-sided stomach and apparent normal situs suggest no inversion.
The image is a single static frame, so peristalsis and emptying cannot be assessed.

clueFacts.fact: A full feeling after small meals (early satiety) fits linitis plastica because cancer infiltrates and stiffens the stomach wall so the stomach cannot stretch to hold food.

clueFacts.clue: just a few bites for months
clueFacts.fact: Fullness after just a few bites for months is typical because linitis plastica often stays silent until it is advanced and most patients present late.
